stem: In a code, consonants are replaced by their mirror-image letter in the alphabet (A and Z swap, B and Y swap, etc.; positions sum to 27), while vowels are shifted 3 places forward. For example, TREND is coded as GIHMW. Using this rule, what is the code for STONE?

per_option_rationale.rationale: S(cons) mirror->H, T(cons) mirror->G, O(vowel)+3=R, N(cons) mirror->M, E(vowel)+3=H, giving HGRMH.
Applying the mirror rule to all letters including vowels: O(15) mirror->L(12) and E(5) mirror->V(22) gives HGLMV.
Swapping the rules (vowels mirrored, consonants +3): S+3=V, T+3=W, O mirror->L, N+3=Q, E mirror->V gives VWLQV.
Using vowel+2 instead of vowel+3: O+2=Q and E+2=G while consonants are mirrored correctly gives HGQMG.

explanation: Identify vowels and consonants in STONE: S(cons), T(cons), O(vowel), N(cons), E(vowel). Mirror consonants (positions sum to 27): S(19)->H(8), T(20)->G(7), N(14)->M(13). Shift vowels +3: O(15)->R(18), E(5)->H(8). Result: H,G,R,M,H = HGRMH. Verify with TREND: T(20)->G(7), R(18)->I(9), E(vowel)+3=H(8), N(14)->M(13), D(4)->W(23) = GIHMW (matches the example).

explanation_sections.punchline: The key setup decision is correctly classifying each letter as vowel or consonant, then applying the correct rule to each class.
explanation_sections.approach: Deductive trace: list each letter of STONE with its type (S-cons, T-cons, O-vowel, N-cons, E-vowel), apply mirror rule to consonants and +3 to vowels, then read off the code.
explanation_sections.lesson: In dual-rule codes, scan the entire word for all vowels before coding - missing even one vowel flips its code to the consonant rule.
explanation_sections.timing: About 85-95 seconds. Fastest check: option 2 has L at position 3 (=O mirrored), immediately confirming the vowel rule was ignored.
